text.p: Germany's Commerzbank said on Sunday that it remained interested in Austria's Creditanstalt-Bankverein but warned that Austria's price expectations had to be realistic.

"Commerzbank has played a continuous role in the past and will in the future if the terms and conditions fit," Commerzbank chief executive Martin Kohlhaussen told a news conference in Washington on Sunday.
Commerzbank is bidding for the bank in a consortium with Italian participation and led by insurer EA-Generali.

The consortium, whose first bid foundered last week because of its reluctance to take on all of Creditanstalt's ordinary shares, is now competing against Die Erste Oesterreichische SparCasse (First Austrian) in a second round.
First Austrian was formerly a partner in the Generali group.

Kohlhaussen said that he believed Austria might however need to become more realistic about the price it hoped to get for the 19.9 million shares it owns in the bank, which makes up 70 percent of its ordinary voting stock.
The government has been targetting a price of 18 billion shillings, based on an assessment by J.P. Morgan. This is well above the current market value of 13 billion schillings.

"We are a private bank," Kohlhaussen said. "Our shareholder policy means acquisitions should be built on solid criteria. There might still be an exaggerated expectation on the price that can be achieved."
He added that a seller must always show some sense of the price a buyer was prepared to pay.
